question: What primary physiological event can occur in the postpartum period before menstruation returns?
explanation: A woman can release an egg and become pregnant again before she sees her first postpartum menstrual period. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h1)

question: Closely spaced pregnancies primarily increase the risk of which maternal outcome?
explanation: Rapid successive pregnancies do not allow the mother's body enough time to replenish vital nutrient stores. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h1)

question: Why are oestrogen-containing contraceptives delayed during the early postpartum period?
explanation: Postpartum women already have a higher tendency for blood clotting, and oestrogen further elevates this thromboembolic risk. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h2)

question: A breastfeeding mother at two weeks postpartum requests a reliable hormonal method that will not interfere with breast milk production. What is the best choice?
explanation: Progestin-only methods do not affect milk volume or quality, making them safe for nursing mothers from day one. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h2)

question: Which contraceptive category provides dual protection against both pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?
explanation: Condoms are the only widely available family planning items that physically block pathogens and sperm simultaneously. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h3)

question: What term describes contraceptive options like implants and intrauterine devices that last for years without daily user action?
explanation: LARC methods provide continuous, highly effective protection without requiring daily attention from the client. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h3)

question: When should a nurse refer a postpartum client to a specialized family planning clinic?

options.A: When the client refuses all forms of infant immunization
options.B: When the infant is exclusively breastfed for one week
options.C: When normal lochia rubra stops by day three
options.D: When the client requests long-acting or surgical methods

explanation: Specialized clinical procedures like IUD insertions or tubal ligations require advanced training available at designated clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h4)

question: What clinical finding represents a major medical restriction for starting combined hormonal contraceptives postpartum?
explanation: Active blood clots contraindicate oestrogen use due to the high risk of fatal pulmonary embolism. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h4)

question: Why is exploring potential side effects during family planning counselling important?

options.A: It prepares the client and reduces early discontinuation
options.B: It proves that hormonal methods are unsafe
options.C: It eliminates the need for any physical examination
options.D: It forces the client to choose permanent sterilization

explanation: Clients who know what to expect are less likely to panic and stop using their chosen method when minor side effects occur. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h5)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a proper family planning counselling session?

options.A: It avoids discussing any potential side effects
options.B: It forces the nurse's preferred method on the client
options.C: It is client-centered and supports informed choice
options.D: It focuses solely on preventing future pregnancies

explanation: Good counselling respects the client's autonomy, values, and personal health goals above all else. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h5)

question: What essential detail must be included in a formal family planning referral letter?

options.B: Home address of the attending nurse
options.C: Complete immunization record of the spouse
options.D: Detailed financial status of the family

explanation: Receiving clinicians need accurate medical and pregnancy details to safely prescribe or insert the requested contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h6)

question: How does thorough pre-referral preparation help improve clinic attendance rates?

options.A: By booking a mandatory taxi service from the ward
options.B: By providing free transportation fare for every single patient
options.C: By ensuring the husband attends every clinic session
options.D: By explaining the location and visit expectations to reduce client anxiety

explanation: Clear guidance on logistics and procedures removes fear and confusion, encouraging patients to follow through with the referral. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h6)

question: A postpartum client refuses a family planning referral, stating her husband disapproves of modern contraceptives. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Invite the partner for joint counselling on reproductive health
options.B: Ignore the objection and refer the client secretly anyway
options.C: Discontinue all postpartum education for this family
options.D: Report the husband to hospital security for non-compliance

explanation: Involving partners helps address misconceptions and fosters collaborative family decision-making regarding reproductive health. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h7)

question: Which strategy is most effective for tracing postpartum clients who miss their scheduled clinic referrals?

options.A: Canceling their hospital health records permanently
options.B: Publishing missed appointment names on public boards
options.C: Utilizing community health workers for follow-up
options.D: Waiting until the next routine pregnancy occurs

explanation: Community health workers bridge the gap between clinics and communities, helping to trace and counsel defaulting clients at home. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h7)
